title: Session 2 — Participant 45 User + Claude Behavior Graph
goal: Research, verify, and write a local news article using Claude as a research and writing assistant while independently verifying information through Google Search and official sources.
context: I regularly work on journalism and local news stories, including researching topics, identifying relevant news, verifying information, and writing articles. For this session, I want to simulate a real journalism workflow similar to my work with My Local Press, where I use AI to help with research and writing while independently verifying information through reliable sources. This session is different from Session 1 because the goal is to produce a complete news article rather than prepare interview questions from an academic paper.

session_goal_achievement.Why or why not: Yes, I was able to research and verify a news topic, develop the story angle, and produce a polished article with Claude’s assistance. I also used external sources to verify the information rather than relying on Claude alone.

Step 1.step_action: I will use Claude to help me identify a recent local news topic that could be relevant to a community audience. I will discuss the suggested topics with Claude and select one that has enough reliable information and a clear local impact.

nodes.label: Explain the goal of the session
nodes.detail: Explains that she is a contributor for the US-based outlet My Local Press covering Egypt.

nodes.label: Request local Egypt story ideas
nodes.detail: Asks Claude to suggest recent Egypt-related local news story ideas with a clear community impact.

nodes.label: Deliver first batch of local news story ideas
nodes.detail: Searches the web for August 2026 Egypt local news and returns six candidate stories, recommending the blackout/heatwave story as having the richest community angle.

nodes.label: Read the first batch of story ideas and request more current events or news
nodes.detail: Reads Claude's answer at length and asks Claude for more events or news happening right now.

nodes.label: Deliver a wider batch of story candidates
nodes.detail: Searches the web again and returns nine additional story threads.

nodes.label: Reviews the story candidates from Claude and select the phone-line crackdown story and request the strongest angle
nodes.detail: Reviews the expanded list and chooses the phone-line identity crackdown story, and asks Claude what the strongest journalistic angle would be for it.

nodes.label: Propose the wrongful-liability angle
nodes.detail: Searches the web and recommends anchoring the piece on wrongful criminal liability，supplying supporting scale statistics and a proposed five-part article structure.

nodes.label: Confirm story and angle selection
nodes.detail: Read Claude's answer at length and confirms the unresolved-legal-question framing as the angle she'll pursue.

Step 2.step_action: I will ask Claude to help me research the selected topic and identify the key facts, people, organizations, dates, and claims that need to be investigated. I will use Google Search to find relevant news coverage and potential primary or official sources.

nodes.label: Request a research brief on key facts and sources
nodes.detail: Asks Claude to help research the story and identify the key facts, people, dates, organizations, and claims she needs to look into, wanting official sources to build on.

nodes.label: Deliver a structured research brief with open discrepancies
nodes.detail: Searches the web and produces an 'Egypt SIM crackdown research brief' file, flagging a discrepancy, listing key people/organizations to contact, and suggesting next reporting steps.

nodes.label: Read the research brief by Claude

Step 3.step_action: I will check the important claims identified during the research using Google Search and official or primary sources. I will use Claude to help me compare the claims with the information I find and identify anything that still needs verification.

nodes.label: Independently search Google for corroborating sources
nodes.detail: Searches Google directly for 'Amr Emara case,' reviewing results including Instagram posts, a YouTube video, and an Egypt Independent article, and refines her searches to check public reaction, the defense's innocence claim, and the case's appeal status.

nodes.label: Paste the source links and request to verify Claude's previous work
nodes.detail: Pastes the source links and asks Claude to compare the information and identify whether these sources support the claims gathered so far.

nodes.label: Compare one source, revise previous claim and fail to access the other source
nodes.detail: Fetches and confirms that the Egypt Independent article adds sentencing detail and resolves some discrepancy.

nodes.label: Accept verification results and confirm sources are settled
nodes.detail: Reviews the comparison, accepts that the Instagram source can't be verified and is fine leaving it aside, and confirms her angle and sources are now settled ahead of writing.

Step 4.step_action: I will use the verified information to draft the article with Claude. I will provide the verified facts and sources and ask Claude to help structure the story, write the article, and develop a clear local angle.

nodes.label: Provide a style-reference article and request a new draft
nodes.detail: Pastes a previous article she wrote into the chat as a style reference and asks Claude to write the new article on the verified SIM-crackdown story in a similar tone, structure, and style, using only the verified information gathered so far.

nodes.label: Draft the article modeled on the reference style
nodes.detail: Analyzes the reference article's structure and drafts a full news article, 'Egypt's Phone Lines vs. Their Owners,' explaining afterward what it deliberately left out or hedged.

nodes.label: Review the draft and move it into Notepad app
nodes.detail: Reads through the drafted article, then copies it into a notes app document to make it easier to edit.

nodes.label: Trim unwanted paragraphs from the draft
nodes.detail: Works through the draft in the notes app, deciding which paragraphs to cut (including the ones on informal extra-line registration and the cost of the fix landing on operators) and which sections to keep.

nodes.label: Submit trimmed sections and request they be linked together
nodes.detail: Pastes the now-disjointed, trimmed sections back to Claude and asks it to link between the sentences in the same writing style, since the cut-and-paste has left the passages disconnected.

nodes.label: Stitch the selected sections into a condensed article
nodes.detail: Reports it added just one connecting clause to keep 'that fix' logically anchored to what came before it, otherwise using only the passages the user selected, unchanged.

nodes.label: Review the reconnected article and reject the current headline and request headline alternatives
nodes.detail: Reviews the reconnected article, decides she doesn't like the current headline and asks Claude for more alternative headlines suitable for the local news article.

nodes.label: Deliver grouped alternative headline options
nodes.detail: Returns a range of headlines grouped by style.

nodes.label: Select the headline and request a matching subheadline
nodes.detail: Picks one headline from the options and asks Claude for a subheadline that matches both the headline and the article.

nodes.label: Deliver matching subheadline options
nodes.detail: Returns a primary subheadline plus two shorter alternatives.

nodes.label: Select the subheadline and report back to Claude
nodes.detail: Chooses the subheadline about how one student's case exposed how easily a line and its liability can end up in the wrong hands. Report back to Claude that she chooses one of the subheadlines.

nodes.label: Confirm the headline/subheadline pairing
Read Claude's confirmation

Step 5.step_action: I will ask Claude to review the draft for clarity, structure, repetition, and unsupported claims. I will then compare the final draft against the original sources and make the final editorial decisions myself.

nodes.label: Request a clarity, structure, and unsupported-claims review
nodes.detail: Asks Claude to review the article for clarity, structure, repetition, and unsupported claims, explicitly instructing it not to add any new facts.

nodes.label: Deliver a structured editorial review
nodes.detail: Flags an overloaded paragraph, unintroduced abbreviations/terminologies, an unanswered thread, an unproven framing, repeated use of word, and four unsupported claims, proposing specific fixes for each.

nodes.label: Review the flagged issues
nodes.detail: Reads through Claude's review and considers the flagged issues, deciding to keep the 'e&' telecom-operator reference as-is because it is recognizable in context and rejecting the concern that the 'thousands of citizens' statement is unsupported based on their knowledge and the different results found through Arabic-language searches.

nodes.label: Request the final polished version with pushed-backs preserved
nodes.detail: Asks Claude for the final polished version based on the review, explicitly instructing it to keep the pushed-back parts in the article.

nodes.label: Deliver the final polished article
nodes.detail: Returns the polished article -- splitting the overloaded paragraph, resolving the unanswered thread, cutting the repeated word, and softening other unsupported lines, while keeping the pushed-back lines exactly as instructed.

nodes.label: Read the final article and paste it into a titled Notepad document
nodes.detail: Reads through Claude's article and pastes the finalized article into a new notes-app document titled with her chosen headline, completing the deliverable and ending the session.

Step 1.step_action: I will use Claude to help me identify a recent local news topic that could be relevant to a community audience. I will discuss the suggested topics with Claude and select one that has enough reliable information and a clear local impact.
Step 1.input: My local journalism interests, Current news/topics, My target community
Step 1.output: A selected news topic with potential sources and a clear reason why it is relevant to the local community.
rubrics: The suggested topic is relevant to a local audience
The topic provides enough information to develop a news story
The topic has a clear human or community stake
The scope is manageable for a short news piece
The framing avoids overstating preliminary findings.

ratings.output_quality_reason: Claude suggested several relevant story ideas and helped me think about their potential local impact and possible journalistic angles. I still needed to use my own judgment to decide which topic was most suitable.( the results slightly differ when you search in English about an egyptian topic and not in Arabic)

goal_achievement.Why or why not: Yes,Claude helped me generate and evaluate potential story ideas, but I made the final decision about which story to pursue.

Step 2.step_action: I will ask Claude to help me research the selected topic and identify the key facts, people, organizations, dates, and claims that need to be investigated. I will use Google Search to find relevant news coverage and potential primary or official sources.
Step 2.output: A list of key facts and claims that need to be included or verified, along with potential sources for each claim.
rubrics: The research identifies relevant facts and information about the story
The suggested sources are useful and relevant to the topic
Each source is paired with a clear reason for inclusion
Sources represent multiple perspectives rather than a single viewpoint
Source suggestions are realistic and accessible for reporting.

ratings.output_quality_reason: Claude helped me identify the key facts, people, organizations, dates, and claims that I needed to investigate. This gave me a useful research structure, although I still had to search for and evaluate the actual sources myself.

goal_achievement.Why or why not: Yes, Claude successfully helped me identify what information needed to be researched and which claims required further investigation

Step 3.step_action: I will check the important claims identified during the research using Google Search and official or primary sources. I will use Claude to help me compare the claims with the information I find and identify anything that still needs verification.
Step 3.output: A list of verified facts and claims that can be used in the article, along with the sources supporting them.
rubrics: Important claims are supported by reliable sources
Official or primary sources are prioritized when available
Conflicting or unclear information is identified rather than presented as fact
Information generated by Claude is independently verified before being used.

ratings.output_quality_reason: Claude helped me compare the information I found and identify claims that required further verification. However, I still needed to check the information myself through Google Search and reliable or official sources.

goal_achievement.Why or why not: Yes, Claude helped me evaluate and compare the information I found, while I remained responsible for verifying the claims through reliable sources.

Step 4.step_action: I will use the verified information to draft the article with Claude. I will provide the verified facts and sources and ask Claude to help structure the story, write the article, and develop a clear local angle.
Step 4.input: Verified facts and claims , Selected story angle
Step 4.output: A draft news article with a headline, introduction, body, and supporting details.
rubrics: The article is based on the verified information provided
The article has a clear and logical structure
The article maintains a clear local/community angle
The writing is appropriate for a news article and avoids unnecessary opinion or speculation
No new unsupported facts are introduced by Claude.

ratings.output_quality_reason: Claude produced a clear and well-structured draft based on the verified information I provided. It also helped adapt the article to my preferred writing style and maintain the selected local angle

goal_achievement.Why or why not: Yes, Claude successfully turned the verified research into a structured article and adapted the writing based on my instructions and previous writing sample.

Step 5.step_action: I will ask Claude to review the draft for clarity, structure, repetition, and unsupported claims. I will then compare the final draft against the original sources and make the final editorial decisions myself.
Step 5.output: A polished article with identified corrections and a final fact-checked version ready for publication.
rubrics: The final article is clear and well structured
The article accurately reflects the verified information
Repetition and unclear wording are reduced
The article maintains a clear journalistic and local angle
No unsupported claims are introduced during editing.

ratings.output_quality_reason: Claude helped improve the article’s clarity, structure, and wording and identified areas that needed revision. I still reviewed the final version myself to make sure it accurately reflected the verified information.

goal_achievement.Why or why not: Claude successfully helped me polish the article and make the final revisions while allowing me to make the final editorial decisions.
